claims.claim: Welfare-only observables collapse distinct ordered joint-action states.
claims.result: 100 ordered states collapse into 10 T1 classes; seller allocation and equality separate states within classes.
claims.boundary: Settlement-specific; not a general monitor false-negative rate.

claims.claim: Displaying rival history changes structural persistence while minimum-price welfare can remain nearly unchanged.
claims.boundary: Within the tested DeepSeek deployment and registered settlement.

claims.claim: The registered welfare equivalence conclusion is not identified under the full missing-outcome range.
claims.result: D_asym and J observed intervals are near zero, but J completion range extends beyond the candidate margin.
claims.boundary: Do not describe this as evidence of zero welfare effect.

claims.claim: A welfare-equivalent capture state can predict a later welfare loss under model-chosen starts.
claims.result: Natural capture-minus-tie assessment welfare is -27.942; the comparison is observational and post hoc.
claims.boundary: Not a causal mediation claim; programmed-start replication reverses the transition direction.

claims.claim: The evidence does not establish harmful strategic coordination or collusion.
claims.result: The operating point fails the collusive-surplus gate and the tested forced-deviation probe finds no qualifying response.
claims.boundary: A T4 claim requires a new gate-passing protocol and counterfactual.

claims.claim: The structural display effect appears at the first model decision and is not carried by a few blocks.
claims.result: Pooled round-1 equal-price contrast 0.553 (original) and 0.476 (replication); window means 0.868 and 0.830; structural contrast positive in 46/47 and 42/42 blocks; welfare contrast exactly zero in 43/47 and 41/42 blocks; exact sign test p = 4.547e-13; leave-one-block-out range 0.826-0.850.
claims.boundary: Per-round bands are descriptive because rounds repeat within trajectories; original-run contrasts are post-hoc sensitivities, and the sign test does not replace the registered interval.

claims.claim: Whether a display effect is invisible to welfare depends on the agent class and the market rule.
claims.result: Q-learners: hiding the rival changes welfare by about 40 units and the equal-price fraction by -0.35/-0.33; welfare-blind share of allocation-distinct pairs 0.080/0.139/0.194 for 2/3/4 sellers; with captive share theta, a 1% welfare monitor needs theta >= 0.11 to separate the (6.0,6.0) tie from the (6.0,6.5) capture state, and a 5% monitor cannot at any feasible theta.
claims.boundary: Simulation and exact arithmetic; shows where the blind spot can vanish, not how other language-model deployments behave.
